t: In front of you is the statue of Field Marshal Alan Brooke, Viscount Alanbrooke, on Whitehall, unveiled in 1993. Brooke was Chief of the Imperial General Staff during the Second World War, the professional head of the British Army, and he was promoted to field marshal on the first of January 1944. The statue is by Ivor Roberts-Jones, a sculptor best known for his heads of notable people such as Yehudi Menuhin. The lettering is credited to David Kindersley, a stone letter-carver who, with his wife Lida Lopes Cardozo, also designed the main gates of the British Library.
